paragraphs: Proponents of later school start times argue that teenagers' biological clocks shift toward later sleeping and waking at puberty, so that an early bell compels students to learn while still physiologically drowsy. Several districts that delayed their start times reported higher attendance and slightly improved grades.

These reports are encouraging, but they should be handled with care. Districts that choose to delay are often those with administrators already committed to improvement, and such districts may have changed other things at the same time. It is conceivable, though untested, that the real gain came from the attention paid to students rather than from the extra sleep. What can be said with some confidence is that nothing in the evidence so far suggests harm.
